cards.text: After the wall was rebuilt, Jerusalem was large and spacious, but there were few people in it (Nehemiah 7:1-4). A big city with hardly anybody home? That's a cookie box with three cookies rattling around in it. Now, friend, people start settling in Jerusalem.

cards.question: The passage opens with one group settling in Jerusalem. Who are they?
The rest of the people cast lots to choose who else moves in. The lots pick ___ out of every ten people to live in Jerusalem.
The text gives Jerusalem a special name as the people the lots pick move in. It calls Jerusalem the ___ city.
After the lots are cast, the other nine out of every ten stay in their own towns.
Some men step up on their own and volunteer to live in Jerusalem. How do the people treat the men who volunteer?

cards.text: Then comes the roll call of who settles in Jerusalem: families from Judah and Benjamin, priests, Levites, and gatekeepers who keep watch at the gates. Most groups get a head count, right down to the last man. I used to count the falling dust back in the junk drawer I got stuck in, friend. I gave up at SEVEN.

Everyone else spreads out over the villages of Judah and Benjamin. Judah's people settle all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom, and Benjamin's settle in towns like Michmash and Bethel. That's not a neighborhood, friend, that's a ROAD TRIP.

Next comes the record of the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua, two of the men the exiles came home with (Ezra 2:2). It follows the priestly families down the generations, with Levites giving praise and thanksgiving as prescribed by David the man of God, all the way to the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe. Generation after generation, somebody wrote down EVERY name. Me? I've got three oven timers going and I can't tell which one is beeping.
That's where we'll leave this city for now, friend. Trust me, Jerusalem's story is NOT done.
